title: Training-Free Cultural Alignment of Large Language Models via Persona Disagreement
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: A frozen model plus persona prompts yields a reliable country-aligned score by keeping a refinement only when two independent runs agree.
layout: 3 colored panels A/B/C, left-to-right, colored arrows tracing personas through pipeline
description: A three-panel figure with rounded, color-coded boxes, read left to right. Panel A (blue) shows a target country and WVS microdata merging into four persona prompts: young, middle-aged and older cohorts and a country-wide aggregate. Each has an avatar icon and its own color. Panel B (orange) sends a shared forced-choice scenario and the four personas plus a base prompt, as colored arrows, through a locked Frozen LLM box. This yields logit gaps δ1–δ4 and δ_base. A dashed box lists 'No weight updates / reward model / target labels'. Panel C (green) has an intuition strip showing two PT-IS runs agreeing or disagreeing on a number line (r≈1 vs r≈0). Below it is the DISCA controller: an ESS-blended anchor, dual-pass refinement, and a reliability gate. These combine into δ_micro and then the country prior δ_final. The eye starts at the colorful persona avatars on the left.
caption: DISCA overview. (A) WVS microdata instantiate four persona prompts for country c: three age cohorts and a country-wide aggregate. (B) The four personas and an unconditioned base prompt run through the frozen model on one scenario, giving the decision-token logit gaps δ1, . . . , δ4 and δbase. (C) The persona-mean gap ¯δ is blended with δbase by the effective sample size (ESS) of the importance weights, giving the consensus anchor. Prospect-Theory importance sampling (PT-IS) runs twice on disjoint half budgets. The squared gap Vr between the two passes sets the reliability gate r = exp(−Vr/s), which scales their average into the gated refinement δ⋆. Anchor plus δ⋆gives the scenario score δmicro (Eq. 6), and the country prior of Eq. 7 turns it into δfinal. Pseudocode in App. A1.
abstract: Large language models now take part in decisions that rest on moral preferences, and those preferences differ by country. A model's default preferences sit closest to one population, so a single deployment serves every country with one country's values. Existing fixes need per-culture training data, a per-country reward model, or access to model internals, which the countries furthest from that default rarely have. We show how far a country can be reached without any of them. Our method, DISCA, keeps the model's weights frozen, sees no country-specific human targets, and reads only the model's score for each answer option. It builds a country as a panel of four persona prompts grounded in World Values Survey microdata. The panel's consensus sets a country-conditioned anchor, a loss-averse refinement beyond that anchor is kept only when two independent runs of it agree, and a running country-level prior pools the decisions already made for the same country. On the 20-country MultiTP benchmark, DISCA lowers misalignment to human preference vectors on all seven frozen backbones we evaluate, by 10 to 24 percent on six of them, and a 14B backbone with DISCA ends closer to the human preferences than a vanilla 70B backbone. DISCA beats every training-free control we test on a shared grid, and on the two backbones where we can replay the exact same model scores it also beats probability averaging, logit consensus and majority vote over the same personas when those rules receive no country prior. Switching each stage off on the logged runs shows that the persona panel and the country-level prior carry most of the gain. Beyond crash dilemmas, DISCA improves social-norm classification on NormAd and moves answers closer to GlobalOpinionQA survey distributions than vanilla decoding does.
